text:
maya: Quick heads up — after the v1->v2 header-fallback change I flipped in staging, the console shows token_cost going up but request_count for the legacy route dropping. dashboard behaved weirdly for a bit. Anyone else see this?

samir: saw a blip too. my hunch is the mapping layer is collapsing some v1 request metadata when we synthesize the v2 route, so metrics aggregation keys don't line up.

olivia: that would explain the UI graphs being discontinuous. product wants a clear story for customers on what ‘compat mode’ will show. we should avoid misleading MBs on quota usage.

toni: +1. observability notes: if route_id changes and we don't carry original client_version tag, telemetry groups under the v2 model and the cost per-request looks inflated because v1 sampling weights differ. we should preserve an orig_version tag or emit a compat_reason label.

kevin: ergonomics idea: add a small console badge on routes that are operating in compatibility-fallback mode with an explanation tooltip and a link to a logs view that shows original headers. that will reduce support tickets.

maya: agreed on the badge. technical question: can we preserve header "x-client-api-version" through the routing proxy and into metrics? right now our header sanitizer drops unknown headers in the fast path.

samir: we can — cost is negligible if we have an allowlist of 3-4 keys and only add them to the post-agg event. but the tricky bit is quotas. Our quota engine currently charges against the effective route (v2) which means customers on legacy plans see quota consumption under a different bucket. that causes the console to show quota used=0 for the legacy route while billing shows tokens consumed.

olivia: that's bad. customers will call support. Any quick mitigations?

toni: short-term: when we detect a header-fallback hit, emit a duplicate telemetry event with original_route="v1" and charge an accounting-only metric so UI can display both views (billing authoritative, UI annotated). longer term we should map quota consumption to both the effective and original route via an aliasing table.

maya: sounds reasonable. can we implement the duplicate event as a non-blocking fire-and-forget in the runtime to avoid latency impact?

samir: yes, runtime can enqueue an async telemetry write. will require a tiny schema bump (add compat_reason and original_route fields). telemetry pipeline needs to accept the extra fields with nulls for normal requests.

kevin: UX thread: how do we present this in rollouts? propose a new console rollout step: "compat telemetry preview" where we show side-by-side metrics for a 24h sample before allowing auto-switch. that would catch anomalies like this.

olivia: product likes the preview step. can we gate it on a client_id allowlist so only affected customers see the preview?

samir: yep. runtime can flag request metadata with client_id and we can surface only those clients in preview.

maya: implementation plan proposal: (1) allowlist header passthrough in proxy (config flag), (2) runtime emits async duplicate telemetry with original_route/orig_version tags, (3) telemetry pipeline accepts compat fields and adds a dashboard panel showing "legacy view vs effective view", (4) console adds a small compat badge + link to preview panel, (5) quota engine: short-term accounting-only aliasing, longer-term canonical mapping in quota v2.

toni: I'll sketch the telemetry schema changes and a migration plan for pipeline consumers. Important: we need to backfill a week of compat events in staging to validate dashboard math.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: compat-telemetry-probe v0.1 to staging on maya/stage.

kevin: re-support: I'll draft the badge copy. suggest "Compatibility routing in effect — some metrics grouped under the effective model. View legacy-vs-effective preview." small copy + link to docs.

olivia: +1. also add a quick note in the planned deprecation docs: "When we route v1->v2, billing will reflect the effective model; dashboard can show legacy usage if compat preview is enabled."

maya: ok i'll open a small RFC for the runtime change and assign samir/toni for telemetry and kevin/olivia for UX + docs. i'll also add a sampling flag so we don't double-write every single request in prod until we validate.

samir: thanks — will pair with maya on the allowlist rollout script.

toni: putting a stub PR for pipeline changes in my queue.

kevin: i'll mock the console badge and preview UI tomorrow and drop screenshots into the RFC thread.

olivia: thanks team. goal: zero-surprise for customers during v1 deprecations. :white_check_mark:

maya: leaving this thread pinned to the RFC until staging validation passes.
